title: SCCM vs Intune - Simply Explained

quotes.text: SCCM is an on-premises tool that you run on your own servers inside your own building on your own network.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives a crisp, plain definition of what SCCM is.

quotes.text: The big difference between SCCM and Intune comes down to just one thing-- infrastructure. SCCM needs a lot of it.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Names the single decisive difference between the two tools.

quotes.text: Intune needs one thing, an internet connection. That's it. No servers, no SQL databases, no distribution points, no management points.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Summarizes the cloud-native advantage of Intune in one punchy line.

quotes.text: Intune can handle roughly 80 to 85% of typical device management scenarios. That's a lot. And for most organizations, Intune alone is enough
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Offers a practical reality check for choosing between the tools.

quotes.text: Co-management is the bridge letting you keep what works while moving towards what's next, but where you start depends entirely on your organization.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Frames co-management as a gradual migration strategy rather than an either-or choice.

takeaways: SCCM is an agent-based on-premises tool with deep control for Windows, OS deployment and servers, but it needs substantial server infrastructure.
Intune is a cloud service that only needs an internet connection, manages Windows, macOS, iOS and Android, and integrates natively with conditional access.
Co-management lets you move workloads such as compliance, endpoint protection and updates to Intune step by step while keeping complex tasks in SCCM.
hook: SCCM and Intune both manage devices, yet they work in completely different ways and picking the wrong one wastes time and money. This episode helps IT admins and decision makers compare on-premises depth with cloud simplicity, understand co-management and choose the right path for their organization.
